title: CPD proposes garment minimum wage of Tk 18,578 to Tk 24,204
excerpt: CPD says the Tk 12,500 entry wage would need to be Tk 16,351 just to keep up with prices since 2023. Workers have asked for Tk 32,000.

image.alt: Finished jeans hanging on a rack in a Bangladesh garment factory
image.credit: Fahad Faisal / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
The garment sector's new minimum wage should be negotiated between a poverty-line wage of Tk 18,578 and a living wage of Tk 24,204 per earner a month, the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) said in a presentation, Determining the Minimum Wage in the RMG Sector, in Dhaka on Wednesday (18 November). The study team was led by Dr Nazneen Ahmed, executive director of CPD.

The current entry wage of Tk 12,500, in force since 1 December 2023, would need to be Tk 16,351 just to keep up with prices, CPD said, as the urban consumer price index rose 30.8% between November 2023 and October 2026. Workers proposed Tk 32,000 at the wage board's second meeting on 9 November; owners have not submitted a proposal.

CPD put the monthly cost of a decent life for a family of four at Tk 38,243, assuming 1.58 earners per family. It also called for a permanent wage commission, a fixed, law-based schedule for setting wages with the next wage board formed by June 2029, and buyers taking part in wage talks.

The wage board's third meeting, postponed on 16 November, has been rescheduled for 23 November.

Why it matters

Garment workers' pay sets living standards for millions of families in Dhaka's industrial belt, where NGOs run health, child care and legal aid services. CPD's numbers give rights groups and the wage board an evidence-based range.

What to watch

The wage board's proposal, the owners' response, and whether a new wage is announced before more factory unrest.

Sources

  • Centre for Policy Dialogue: Determining the Minimum Wage in the RMG Sector, 18 November 2026 (PDF)
